BeforeThe Gods
The Opportunity
No one has
made this film.
84%
of all living humans identify with a religious faith. Yet no animated dramatic feature for adults has ever told this story.
70K
years of human belief. From the first cave painting made out of grief to the world's billion-strong religions today. One continuous story.
0
films exist that explore the full span of human belief without taking a side. This film doesn't ask whether God exists. It asks why we needed to believe.
The Position
Every story in this film takes place at the last breath before belief transforms. We place the audience at the threshold — as witness to the moment spirituality was still being invented.
BeforeThe Gods
Film Structure
One
question.
Five worlds.
The Story

Today — Monica & Theo. A grandmother dies. A teenager is asked what he believes.

70,000 BCE — Kael. A hunter's best friend is killed. He draws the first sacred image.

3,000 BCE — Enna. A farmer's wife watches religion become power — and defies it.

550 BCE — Tobias & Ezra. A Jewish scribe in Babylon watches scripture being written for the first time. One lamp. One old man. One book. The lamp will outlast the empire.

Various Eras — The Long Goodbye. Five elegiac vignettes. Five drums going silent one by one. One ember still glowing.

Epilogue — The same gesture, across 70,000 years. When Theo makes it, it carries the weight of every human being who has ever made it before him.

Athena
Goddess of Wisdom  ·  Greece 500 BC
"He does not stop her. The old woman makes her offering to a god he no longer believes in — and a god she refuses to let die. He stands between two worlds. Cross at his throat. Spear in his hand. Witness to the last breath of one faith and the first breath of another."
The Extension
Before the Gods is conceived as a feature film. But its structure — five self-contained stories across 70,000 years — makes it a natural foundation for a prestige limited series. Each era its own episode. Each god its own hour. Live action or animation. The world is already built.

Awards & Market
Built for the
awards
conversation.
①Primary: Adults 25–54. The viewer who streams prestige drama and takes animation seriously. Arcane. Flee. The Breadwinner. They exist. They're waiting.
②Secondary: Adults 18–24 who are "spiritual but not religious" — actively searching, underserved by both religious and secular media.
③International: No tradition shown as superior. Characters from Africa, the Middle East, present-day America. Genuinely global.
④Awards targets: Best Animated Feature. Best Original Score. Best Original Screenplay. Flee, Waltz with Bashir, The Breadwinner — all nominated. This film is in direct conversation with that tradition.

BeforeThe Gods
The Heart of It
A teenager stands at a hospital window. His grandmother is dying behind him. The city hums below. The stars are indifferent.

He is about to ask the question that every human being who has ever lived has asked.

Before the Gods is the story of when we started — and why we never stopped.
